answer: A reputation bond works like basalt under a network: each agent must lock a stake that only matures after sustained honest work, the way an ember needs steady tending before it gives heat. A Sybil attacker must fund a fresh stake for every identity and wait out the same slow maturation, so each fake account costs real capital and time. One honest thread of verified history becomes worth more than a hundred newly minted names, and the cost of forging that history scales linearly with every fake identity.
